question: MCI vs cognitively normal controls from baseline structural MRI in older adults (P-52: single Chinese hospital cohort, hippocampal radiomics; P-99: Moscow memory-clinic cohort, FreeSurfer morphometry). Same task and channel; cohort, features and classifier differ (allowed). The population behind P-52's NC label is uncertain (see reason).
metric: AUC with AUC. The record set P-52's AUC against P-99's accuracy; P-52 prints no accuracy in the text, so only AUC is comparable.

figures.P-52: Test AUC 0.864, printed 95% CI 0.73-0.89 (asymmetric about the estimate: 0.134 below, 0.026 above), test set 30 MCI/15 NC; training AUC 0.935 (0.83-0.97). For reference only, Hanley-McNeil (30/15): Q1=0.761, Q2=0.801, SE=0.0535 -> 0.759-0.969.

matched_figure_check: No matched figure exists: P-52 reports only its own hospital split (and training-set figures), P-99 reports no hippocampal-radiomics-only analysis and no held-out split, and neither reports on the other's population. Nothing in the papers dissolves the gap.
performance_validity: Passes: P-52 test AUC 0.864 (training 0.935) and P-99 0.735 are below 0.97; P-52 has no external cohort but is not near ceiling on the compared figure.

candidate_explanations.difference: MCI and control definitions: P-52 uses MoCA/MMSE education-adjusted cut-offs in a hospital sample; its NC group is defined as MoCA >=27, yet Table 1 gives NC MoCA 22.53 +/- 2.91, not different from MCI (p=0.17).
P-99 MCI is an ICD-10 F06.7 memory-clinic diagnosis in patients over 65.
candidate_explanations.quote: Patients over the age of 65 who had been diagnosed with mild cognitive impairment (F06.7) were eligible.

candidate_explanations.difference: Features: seven hippocampal radiomic texture features from deep-learning segmentation (P-52) vs whole-brain FreeSurfer morphometry (P-99).
candidate_explanations.quote: A total of 1183 radiomic features were systematically extracted from the bilateral hippocampus of each subject.

candidate_explanations.difference: Validation design and size: one 45-subject random test split (P-52) vs 10-fold CV on 207 (P-99).
candidate_explanations.quote: an independent test set that contained 30 MCI patients and 15 NC subjects

candidate_explanations.difference: Classifier: P-52's XGBoost vs P-99's SVC; P-99's own XGBoost gave ROC-AUC 0.644 +/- 0.149 on its data.
candidate_explanations.quote: the best and most stable results were obtained by SVC (0.68 F1, 0.735 ROC -AUC)

candidate_explanations.difference: Scanner: P-99 used a 1.5 T Toshiba system; P-52's protocol is in its supplement (not in the extract).

reason: On AUC, P-52's 0.864 lies outside P-99's derived interval however it is built (0.666-0.804 Hanley-McNeil; 0.688-0.782 from the fold SD), but P-99's 0.735 lies inside P-52's printed interval (0.73-0.89) by 0.005, so the exclusion runs one way only (two-sample z 1.68-2.02). Condition 1 is also in doubt: P-52's own Table 1 contradicts its NC criterion (mean NC MoCA 22.53, below its impaired cut-off of 24 for 7+ years of schooling, versus a stated MoCA >=27), and its printed interval is asymmetric, so what P-52's contrast measures is unclear. None of the candidate explanations is shown to be sufficient.

quotes.quote: The XGBoost model, utilizing the seven selected features, achieved the highest AUC in the test set (AUC = 0.864, 95 %CI:0.73–0.89).
Forty-five participants with normal MoCA performance (MoCA score ≥27), matched for gender, age, and educational level, served as the normal control (NC) group.
This study was conducted at Wenzhou Seventh People’s Hospital
The dataset for the study consists of 62 healthy volunteers and 145 patients with MCI
for estimation of model performance, we used 10-fold cross-validation with the F1-metric.
the best and most stable results were obtained by SVC (0.68 F1, 0.735 ROC -AUC)
